citations.narrative:
During inspection, the licensee was unable to provide documentation of required annual veterinary examinations and
findings conducted within the last 12 months on 45 adult dogs present in the facility
Annual veterinary examinations are important for evaluating the health of all breeding stock and adult animals to detect
diseases and conditions that may impact their well-being.
An annual veterinary examination is required for all adult dogs within a licensed facility and should include a record of
exam findings for each individual animal dated and signed by your veterinarian.
Correct by December 15 2026

During inspection, the licensee was unable to provide documentation of required annual sampling and test results for
fecal parasite testing and heartworm testing for adult dogs in the facility. No adult dogs have been tested within the past
12 months.
Annual testing for intestinal parasites and heartworm is important for detecting underlying parasite issues that may
adversely impact the health and well-being of adult dogs in the facility.
Sampling and treatment of parasites in accordance with a schedule approved by the attending veterinarian is required.
Correct by December 15, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
